intro:
Ethos allows the addition of Lua scripts by the user to extend its features.

The Lua interpreter embedded inside Ethos is based on Lua 5.4.3, it is packaged with those libraries:

- basic library
- `table` library
- `io` library
- `os` library
- `string` library
- `math` library

The os library has been modified a little bit and offers those functions:

- `os.stat()` Check if a file / directory exists and retrieve its infos
- `os.remove()` Remove a file or an empty directory
- `os.rename()` Rename a file or a directory
- `os.rmtree()` Remove a whole directory with all its files and subdirectories
- `os.mkdir()` Create an empty directory
- `os.copy()` Copy a file / directory to another directory

The file paths may start with following prefixes:

- `AUDIO:` Audio directory (before the language)
- `VOICEx:` Audio directory (after the language and voice)
- `BITMAPS:` User bitmaps directory
- `SCRIPTS:` Lua scripts directory
- `SCREENSHOTS:` Screenshots directory
- `LOGS:` Logs directory

members.name: value
members.brief: Return the source value / Set the source value on Lua sources / Vars / Telemetry sensors.
examples:
source = system.getSource({name="GPS", options=OPTION_LATITUDE})
print(source:value())

source = system.getSource("LiPo", options=OPTION_CELLS_COUNT)
print(source:value())
source = system.getSource("LiPo")
print(source:value({options=OPTION_CELLS_COUNT}))
print(source:value({options=OPTION_CELL_INDEX(1)}))

source = system.getSource({category=CATEGORY_CHANNEL, member=0})
print(source:value({options=OPTION_CHANNEL_OUTPUT+OPTION_CHANNEL_PWM}))

source = system.getSource("MySensor")
print(source:value()) -- get the value of MySensor

members.name: reset

source1 = system.getSource("ALT")
source1:reset()
source2 = system.getSource({category=CATEGORY_TIMER, member=0})

members.name: registerWidget

params.description:
table with elements:

- `key` (string): unique key, with 7 chars max
- `name` (string or function): widget name
- `create` (function, optional): handler called when the widget is added to the model (created / read from storage), it will return the widget which is passed later to all functions
- `destroy` (function, optional): handler called on widget deletion
- `configure` (function, optional): handler called on widget configuration
- `build` (function, optional): handler called when the widget is built in the Home screen, after creation and configuration
- `wakeup` (function, optional): handler called at each loop
- `event` (function, optional): handler called when an event is received (event not passed to the parent window if the handler returns True)
- `paint` (function): paint function
- `menu` (function, optional): handler called when the contextual menu is created, to allow adding more options to the menu, the handler should return a table of pairs { name, function }
- `read` (function, optional): optional read handler
- `write` (function, optional): optional write handler
- `persistent` (boolean, optional): persistent data
- `title` (boolean, optional): title forced ON / OFF
params.name: params

examples:
-- Lua Sinus widget
local translations = {en="Lua Sinus", fr="Sinus Lua"}

local function name(widget)
    local locale = system.getLocale()
    return translations[locale] or translations["en"]
end

local function create()
    return {color=lcd.RGB(0, 0, 255)}
end

local function paint(widget)
    local w, h = lcd.getWindowSize()
    lcd.drawLine(0, h/2, w, h/2)
    lcd.color(widget.color)
    for i = 0,w do
      local val = math.sin(i*math.pi/(w/2))
      lcd.drawPoint(i, val*h/2+h/2)
    end
end

local function init()
    system.registerWidget({key="sinus", name=name, create=create, paint=paint})
end

return {init=init}

members.name: registerSensor
members.brief: Register an S.Port sensor definition, so that it gets recognized (name, unit, decimals, protocol min/max) when the sensors Discover finds an appId in this range, instead of falling back to a generic unnamed sensor.

params.description:
table with elements:

- `manufacturer` (string, optional): restricts this definition to models that have this manufacturer selected (Model / Edit) - omit it to make the definition usable regardless of the model's manufacturer choice
- `appIdStart` (integer): first S.Port appId this definition matches
- `appIdEnd` (integer, optional): last S.Port appId this definition matches (defaults to `appIdStart`, ie a single appId)
- `name` (string): sensor name
- `unit` (integer, optional): sensor unit (UNIT_* constant, defaults to UNIT_NONE)
- `decimals` (integer, optional): number of decimals (defaults to 0)
- `min` (number, optional): protocol minimum value, in display units (eg 100.0 with 1 decimal is stored as 1000)
- `max` (number, optional): protocol maximum value, in display units
- `userMin` (number, optional): user-editable minimum value, in display units (defaults to `min`)
- `userMax` (number, optional): user-editable maximum value, in display units (defaults to `max`)
- `onDiscover` (function, optional): handler called with the newly created sensor's source, when the sensors Discover creates it
params.name: params

examples: system.registerSensor({appIdStart=0x5150, appIdEnd=0x515F, name="My sensor", unit=UNIT_VOLT, decimals=2, min=0, max=42.0})

members.name: registerTask

params.description:
table with elements:

- `key` (string, 7 chars max): task key
- `name` (string or function): task name
- `init` (function, optional): handler called on task init
- `done` (function, optional): handler called on task stop
- `event` (function, optional): handler called at each event
- `wakeup` (function, optional): handler called at each loop
- `read` (function, optional): optional read handler
- `write` (function, optional): optional write handler
- `configure` (function, optional): handler called on task configuration
params.name: params

examples:
local function taskName()
  return "My task name"
end

local function taskInit()
  print("Task Init ...")
end

local function taskWakeup()
  print("Task Wakeup ...")
end

local function taskEvent(event)
  print("Task Event", event)
end

local function init()
  system.registerTask({key="LuaTask", name=taskName, init=taskInit, wakeup=taskWakeup, event=taskEvent})
end

return {init=init}
